options.label: B
options.text: Compression ultrasound of the affected leg

explanation: Compression ultrasound is the preferred initial imaging test for suspected deep vein thrombosis, especially in patients with recent surgery and localized symptoms.

sharedCase: A 58-year-old man presents with unilateral leg swelling and pain for 3 days. He has no dyspnea or chest pain. He underwent knee replacement surgery 2 weeks ago.
stem: Which factors increase the pretest probability of deep vein thrombosis? Select ALL that apply.
explanation: Major surgery, malignancy, unilateral swelling, and immobility are established risk factors for venous thromboembolism.

vignette: A 64-year-old woman presents with sudden onset dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain. Blood pressure is stable. Clinical probability for pulmonary embolism is low.
stem: What is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: In patients with low clinical probability, a negative D-dimer can safely exclude pulmonary embolism without imaging.

stem: Which situations allow venous thromboembolism to be excluded without imaging? Select ONE

options.text: High clinical probability with negative D-dimer
Low or moderate clinical probability with negative D-dimer
Isolated calf pain without risk factors

explanation: A negative D-dimer in patients with low or moderate clinical probability reliably excludes venous thromboembolism.

vignette: A 71-year-old man is diagnosed with proximal deep vein thrombosis. He has stable renal function and no active cancer.
stem: Which initial treatment is most appropriate?

options.label: B
options.text: Low molecular weight heparin followed by oral anticoagulation

explanation: Initial treatment of confirmed deep vein thrombosis requires therapeutic anticoagulation, typically with low molecular weight heparin followed by oral therapy.

sharedCase: A 71-year-old man is diagnosed with proximal deep vein thrombosis. He has stable renal function and no active cancer.
stem: Which anticoagulants are appropriate for initial treatment of venous thromboembolism? Select ALL that apply
explanation: Initial therapy includes parenteral anticoagulants and selected direct oral anticoagulants. Acetylsalicylic acid alone is insufficient.

vignette: A 55-year-old woman experiences a first episode of provoked deep vein thrombosis following surgery.
stem: What is the recommended duration of anticoagulation?
explanation: A first venous thromboembolism associated with a transient risk factor is treated for 3 months.

sharedCase: A 55-year-old woman experiences a first episode of provoked deep vein thrombosis following surgery.
stem: Which scenarios support extended or indefinite anticoagulation? Select ALL that apply.

options.text: First provoked distal deep vein thrombosis

explanation: Recurrent unprovoked events, malignancy, and persistent risk factors justify extended anticoagulation.

vignette: A pregnant woman is diagnosed with acute pulmonary embolism.
stem: Which anticoagulant is preferred?
explanation: Low molecular weight heparin is the anticoagulant of choice during pregnancy as it does not cross the placenta.

sharedCase: A pregnant woman is diagnosed with acute pulmonary embolism.
stem: Which anticoagulants should not be used during pregnancy? Select ALL that apply.
explanation: Warfarin and direct oral anticoagulants are contraindicated in pregnancy.
Fondaparinux is reserved only when other agents cannot be used.

explanation: Alpha blockade first.

In pheochromocytoma, phenoxybenzamine (or a selective alpha-1 blocker) is given for 1–2 weeks before surgery. A beta blocker given first leaves alpha-mediated vasoconstriction unopposed and can cause a hypertensive crisis.

vignette: A 34-year-old woman has gained 12 kg over a year, with wide purple abdominal striae, proximal muscle weakness, and new hypertension. She takes no medications.
stem: Which of the following is the best initial test?
explanation: Overnight low-dose dexamethasone suppression test.

First establish hypercortisolism using one of: 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression, late-night salivary cortisol, or 24-hour urine free cortisol. ACTH and imaging come afterwards to find the source.

vignette: A 45-year-old woman with Addison disease has had gastroenteritis for 2 days and has not kept her medications down. Blood pressure is 78/44 mm Hg, sodium 126 mEq/L, potassium 5.9 mEq/L, glucose 58 mg/dL.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate treatment?

options.label: B
options.text: IV hydrocortisone and IV normal saline

options.label: C
options.text: Cosyntropin stimulation test, then treat based on result

explanation: IV hydrocortisone and saline.
This is adrenal crisis: hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia in a patient who missed steroids during illness. Treat at once; do not delay for testing.

vignette: A 29-year-old asymptomatic woman has calcium of 11.2 mg/dL on routine testing. PTH is mildly elevated. Her mother also has "high calcium." 24-hour urine calcium is very low, with a calcium-to-creatinine clearance ratio below 0.01.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
explanation: Reassurance.

Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia is caused by an inactivating mutation of the calcium-sensing receptor. Mild hypercalcemia, normal or slightly raised PTH, and very low urine calcium distinguish it from primary hyperparathyroidism. It is benign and surgery does not help.

vignette: A 29-year-old woman has 8 months of amenorrhea and galactorrhea. Pregnancy test is negative, TSH is normal, prolactin is 180 ng/mL. MRI shows an 8-mm pituitary adenoma.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Cabergoline.
Dopamine agonists are first-line for prolactinomas of any size; they lower prolactin and shrink the tumor. Surgery is for patients who fail or cannot tolerate medical therapy.

vignette: A 41-year-old woman has anterior neck pain radiating to the jaw, palpitations, and tremor 3 weeks after a viral upper respiratory infection. The thyroid is exquisitely tender. TSH is suppressed, free T4 is high, ESR is 88 mm/h, and radioactive iodine uptake is very low.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: NSAID and beta blocker.

Subacute (de Quervain) thyroiditis follows a viral illness and causes a painful gland, high ESR, and low iodine uptake because preformed hormone is leaking out. Antithyroid drugs do not work because no new hormone is being made.

vignette: A 61-year-old man with type 2 diabetes takes metformin. HbA1c is 8.1%. He has heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and an eGFR of 48 mL/min/1.73 m².
stem: Which of the following is the best medication to add?
explanation: SGLT2 inhibitor.

In type 2 diabetes with heart failure or chronic kidney disease, an SGLT2 inhibitor reduces heart-failure hospitalization and slows kidney disease regardless of HbA1c. Pioglitazone worsens heart failure.

vignette: A 15-year-old boy has 3 hours of sudden severe left scrotal pain and vomiting. The left testis is high-riding with a horizontal lie, and the cremasteric reflex is absent.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: A
options.text: Scrotal ultrasound with Doppler, then decide

explanation: Immediate surgical exploration.

The picture is classic for testicular torsion. Salvage falls quickly after about 6 hours, so when clinical suspicion is high, surgery is not delayed for imaging. Both testes are fixed (orchiopexy) at operation.

vignette: A 67-year-old man has a weak stream, hesitancy, and nocturia three times a night. The prostate is smooth, symmetric, and enlarged. Urinalysis is normal. He wants relief as quickly as possible.
stem: Which of the following is the best initial drug?
explanation: Tamsulosin.
Alpha-1 blockers relax prostatic and bladder-neck smooth muscle and work within days. 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors shrink the gland but take 6–12 months. Anticholinergics can provoke retention.

vignette: A 34-year-old man has colicky right flank pain. CT without contrast shows a 4-mm stone in the distal right ureter with mild hydronephrosis. He is afebrile, creatinine is normal, urinalysis shows only blood, and pain is controlled with ketorolac.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.label: D
options.text: Hydration, analgesia, tamsulosin, and straining the urine

explanation: Conservative management.

Ureteral stones of 5 mm or less usually pass on their own. With no infection, normal kidney function, and controlled pain, treat with fluids, NSAIDs, and an alpha blocker, and strain the urine to analyze the stone.

vignette: A 58-year-old woman with diabetes has left flank pain, temperature of 39.4°C, and blood pressure of 92/58 mm Hg. CT shows a 9-mm obstructing proximal ureteral stone with hydronephrosis. Urinalysis shows many white cells and bacteria. Antibiotics and fluids are started.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: A
options.text: Urgent decompression with ureteral stent or percutaneous nephrostomy

explanation: Urgent decompression.
An obstructed, infected kidney is an emergency: antibiotics cannot reach a closed space. Drain first with a stent or nephrostomy; definitive stone treatment waits until the infection has cleared.

vignette: A 62-year-old man with a 40-pack-year smoking history has two episodes of painless visible blood in the urine. Urine culture is negative. CT urography shows normal kidneys and ureters.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: Cystoscopy.
Painless gross hematuria in an older smoker is bladder cancer until proven otherwise. Evaluation is upper-tract imaging plus cystoscopy; cytology alone is not sensitive enough.

vignette: A 27-year-old man notices a painless, firm lump in the right testis. Ultrasound shows a 2-cm solid hypoechoic intratesticular mass. Serum tumor markers are drawn.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: Radical inguinal orchiectomy.
A solid intratesticular mass is treated as cancer. Removal through the groin is both diagnosis and treatment. Any trans-scrotal approach risks seeding the scrotum and altering lymphatic spread.

vignette: A 22-year-old sexually active man has 3 days of gradually worsening right scrotal pain and dysuria. The epididymis is tender and swollen, the cremasteric reflex is present, and pain improves when the scrotum is lifted.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Ceftriaxone plus doxycycline.

In sexually active men under 35, epididymitis is usually from chlamydia or gonorrhea. In older men, or those who practise insertive anal sex, enteric organisms are more likely and a fluoroquinolone is used.

vignette: A 72-year-old man with known prostate enlargement took diphenhydramine for sleep. He now has been unable to urinate for 10 hours and has severe lower abdominal pain. A tender suprapubic mass is felt.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: B
options.text: CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis

explanation: Bladder catheterization.

Acute urinary retention needs prompt decompression. Anticholinergic and antihistamine drugs are common triggers in men with prostate enlargement. An alpha blocker is then started before a trial without catheter.

vignette: A 24-year-old man with sickle cell disease has had a painful, rigid erection for 5 hours. The glans is soft. Cavernosal blood gas shows pH 7.18, PO2 24 mm Hg.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Aspiration and phenylephrine.

Hypoxic, acidotic cavernosal blood means ischemic (low-flow) priapism, a compartment syndrome of the penis. After 4 hours it needs aspiration and an alpha agonist to prevent fibrosis and erectile dysfunction.

vignette: A 30-year-old man is brought in after a motor vehicle crash with a pelvic fracture. There is blood at the urethral meatus and a perineal hematoma. He cannot void.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: Retrograde urethrography.

Blood at the meatus, perineal bruising, inability to void, or a high-riding prostate after pelvic fracture suggests urethral injury. The urethra is imaged before any catheter is passed, because blind catheterization can turn a partial tear into a complete one.

vignette: A 44-year-old man has 2 days of severe low back pain, numbness around the anus and inner thighs, bilateral leg weakness, and has not urinated for 14 hours.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: C
options.text: Emergency MRI of the lumbar spine

explanation: Emergency MRI.

Saddle numbness, bilateral leg weakness, and urinary retention mean cauda equina syndrome. It needs urgent MRI and surgical decompression; delay risks permanent bladder, bowel, and sexual dysfunction.

vignette: A 23-year-old man falls on an outstretched hand. He has tenderness in the anatomic snuffbox. Wrist X-rays, including a scaphoid view, are normal.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.label: A
options.text: Elastic bandage and return to sport

options.label: B
options.text: Thumb spica splint and repeat imaging in 10–14 days

explanation: Thumb spica splint and repeat imaging.

Scaphoid fractures are often invisible on first X-rays. Because the blood supply enters distally, a missed fracture risks avascular necrosis of the proximal pole and nonunion. Treat as a fracture until proven otherwise (MRI is an alternative for early confirmation).

vignette: A 26-year-old man had a closed tibial shaft fracture splinted 6 hours ago. He now has severe leg pain not relieved by morphine, and pain increases sharply when his toes are passively extended. Pedal pulses are palpable.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: A
options.text: Elevate the leg and re-examine in 4 hours

explanation: Emergency fasciotomy.
Pain out of proportion and pain on passive stretch are the earliest signs of compartment syndrome. Pulses are usually still present; loss of pulse is a late sign. The diagnosis is clinical.

vignette: A 13-year-old obese boy has 3 weeks of limp and left knee pain. Knee examination is normal. The left hip has limited internal rotation, and the thigh rotates outward when the hip is flexed.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
explanation: Non-weight-bearing and surgical fixation.

Slipped capital femoral epiphysis presents in obese adolescents, often as referred knee pain. Obligatory external rotation on hip flexion is typical. The hip is pinned in place to stop further slip and avascular necrosis.

vignette: A 58-year-old man with diabetes has 2 days of a hot, swollen, very painful right knee and a temperature of 38.7°C. He cannot tolerate any movement of the joint.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: Arthrocentesis.
An acutely hot, swollen joint with fever is septic arthritis until joint fluid proves otherwise. Fluid is sent for cell count, Gram stain, culture, and crystals before antibiotics are given.

vignette: A 35-year-old man has 4 days of low back pain after lifting a heavy box. There is no fever, weight loss, trauma, weakness, numbness, or bladder change. Examination shows paraspinal muscle tenderness and a normal neurologic exam.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
explanation: NSAIDs and staying active.
Acute low back pain without red flags is not imaged in the first 4–6 weeks. Most cases resolve on their own. Bed rest slows recovery.

vignette: A 21-year-old man has an anterior shoulder dislocation after a fall.
stem: Before reduction, which finding should be specifically looked for?

options.label: A
options.text: Loss of sensation over the lateral shoulder

options.label: C
options.text: Loss of sensation over the little finger

explanation: Sensation over the lateral shoulder.
The axillary nerve runs around the surgical neck of the humerus and is the nerve most often injured in anterior dislocation. It supplies the deltoid and the skin over it.

vignette: A 68-year-old woman has a new vertebral compression fracture after bending to pick up a bag. Bone density shows a T-score of −2.8 at the hip. Calcium, vitamin D, creatinine, and TSH are normal.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Alendronate.

A fragility fracture of the spine or hip, or a T-score of −2.5 or lower, is an indication for drug treatment. Oral bisphosphonates are first-line. Calcium and vitamin D are added but are not enough alone.

vignette: A 32-year-old pregnant woman has numbness and tingling of the thumb, index, and middle fingers that wake her at night and improve when she shakes her hand. Strength is normal.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

options.label: D
options.text: Night-time wrist splint in neutral position

explanation: Night-time wrist splint.
Carpal tunnel syndrome is common in pregnancy and usually improves after delivery. Splinting is first-line; injection or surgery is for persistent or severe disease with weakness or thenar wasting.

vignette: A 22-year-old soccer player plants her foot and pivots, feels a "pop" in the knee, and has swelling within an hour. The Lachman test shows increased forward movement of the tibia with a soft end point.
stem: Which structure is most likely injured?
explanation: Anterior cruciate ligament.

A non-contact pivot injury with a pop and rapid swelling (blood in the joint) plus a positive Lachman test indicates ACL tear. Meniscal tears swell more slowly and cause locking or catching. MRI confirms.

vignette: A 46-year-old woman has an 8-mm pigmented lesion on her back that has grown over 6 months. It is asymmetric with irregular borders and several shades of brown and black.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: Excisional biopsy with narrow margins.

A lesion suspicious for melanoma is removed whole with 1–3 mm margins so the pathologist can measure depth (Breslow thickness), the main factor in prognosis and in how wide the later re-excision must be. A shave biopsy may cut through the base and lose the depth.

vignette: A 31-year-old woman started lamotrigine 2 weeks ago. She has fever, painful erosions of the lips and mouth, red eyes, and dusky skin lesions with blistering and sloughing over about 8% of her body. Light rubbing separates the skin.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: A
options.text: Stop lamotrigine and admit for supportive care, ideally in a burn unit

explanation: Stop the drug and admit.

Stevens–Johnson syndrome (under 10% of body surface) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (over 30%) usually start 1–3 weeks after a new drug: anticonvulsants, sulfonamides, allopurinol, NSAIDs. Stopping the drug and burn-style supportive care are the key steps.

vignette: A 29-year-old man has well-demarcated red plaques with thick silvery scale on both elbows and knees, covering about 3% of his body. Fingernails show pitting.
stem: Which of the following is the best initial treatment?
explanation: High-potency topical corticosteroid.

Limited plaque psoriasis is treated topically, often with a vitamin D analog added. Systemic agents and biologics are for extensive disease or psoriatic arthritis. Oral steroids are avoided because stopping them can trigger a severe flare.

vignette: A 19-year-old woman has severe nodulocystic acne with scarring that has not responded to topical retinoids and 4 months of oral doxycycline. Isotretinoin is planned.
stem: Which of the following is required before starting?

options.label: C
options.text: Pregnancy testing and two forms of contraception

explanation: Pregnancy testing and contraception.

Isotretinoin is a severe teratogen. Patients who can become pregnant need two negative pregnancy tests before starting, monthly testing, and two forms of contraception. Lipids and liver enzymes are also monitored.

vignette: A 70-year-old farmer has a slowly growing, pearly papule with rolled borders and fine surface blood vessels on the side of his nose. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Mohs surgery.
Basal cell carcinoma rarely spreads but invades locally. On the face, Mohs surgery gives the highest cure rate while sparing tissue.

vignette: A 78-year-old man has very itchy, tense blisters on his thighs and trunk. The blisters do not rupture easily and his mouth is clear.
stem: Which finding is expected on direct immunofluorescence of skin beside a blister?

options.label: B
options.text: Linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane

options.label: C
options.text: Granular IgA at the tips of the dermal papillae

options.label: E
options.text: Granular IgM at the dermal–epidermal junction only

explanation: Linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane.

Bullous pemphigoid affects older adults, with tense, itchy blisters and spared mucosa; antibodies target hemidesmosomes. Pemphigus vulgaris gives flaccid blisters, mouth erosions, and a net-like pattern between cells.

vignette: A 33-year-old man returns from camping in Connecticut. He has a 12-cm expanding red patch with central clearing on his thigh, fatigue, and mild joint aches.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: A
options.text: Lyme serology and treat only if positive

explanation: Oral doxycycline.
Erythema migrans in an endemic area is a clinical diagnosis. Serology is often negative this early and is not needed. IV ceftriaxone is for neurologic disease or high-grade heart block.

vignette: A 6-year-old boy has a scaly patch of hair loss on the scalp with broken hairs appearing as black dots, and tender nodes at the back of the neck.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Oral griseofulvin.
Tinea capitis involves the hair shaft, which topical drugs do not reach. Oral griseofulvin or terbinafine is needed. Antifungal shampoo can be added to reduce spread.

vignette: A 2-year-old girl with atopic dermatitis develops fever and clusters of small blisters and punched-out erosions with crusting over her eczema on the cheeks and arms.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Acyclovir.

Eczema herpeticum is herpes simplex spreading across skin affected by atopic dermatitis. It can be life-threatening and needs prompt antiviral treatment. If lesions are near the eye, an eye examination is needed.

vignette: A 68-year-old fair-skinned man has several rough, sandpaper-like, scaly papules on his bald scalp and the backs of his hands.
stem: If untreated, these lesions may progress to which of the following?
explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma.
Actinic keratoses are caused by long-term sun exposure and are precursors of squamous cell carcinoma. They are treated with cryotherapy when few, or with topical fluorouracil when many.

vignette: A 72-year-old woman has 2 weeks of right-sided headache, scalp tenderness, pain in the jaw when chewing, and a brief episode of vision loss in the right eye this morning. ESR is 95 mm/h.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: A
options.text: Temporal artery biopsy, then treat if positive

explanation: High-dose glucocorticoids at once.
Giant cell arteritis threatens permanent blindness. Steroids are started on clinical suspicion; biopsy remains positive for 1–2 weeks after treatment begins, so it never delays treatment.

vignette: A 66-year-old man with stage 4 chronic kidney disease wakes with severe pain, redness, and swelling of the right big toe. Joint fluid shows needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals; Gram stain is negative.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.label: B
options.text: Allopurinol started today as the only treatment

explanation: Glucocorticoid.

In acute gout with advanced kidney disease, NSAIDs are avoided and colchicine needs major dose reduction, so a steroid injection or short oral course is preferred. Urate-lowering therapy does not treat the acute attack.

vignette: A 38-year-old woman has 4 months of pain and swelling in the knuckles and middle finger joints of both hands and both wrists, with morning stiffness lasting 2 hours. Anti-CCP antibody is positive.
stem: Which of the following is the best initial long-term treatment?
explanation: Methotrexate.

A disease-modifying drug is started as soon as rheumatoid arthritis is diagnosed to prevent joint erosion; methotrexate is first choice. NSAIDs and steroids relieve symptoms only. Biologics are added if methotrexate fails.

vignette: A 58-year-old woman taking hydralazine for 10 months has joint pains, pleuritic chest pain, and low-grade fever. ANA is positive. There is no kidney or nervous system involvement.
stem: Which antibody is most likely to be present?
explanation: Anti-histone.

Drug-induced lupus (hydralazine, procainamide, isoniazid, minocycline, TNF inhibitors) causes joint pain, serositis, and fever, usually sparing the kidneys and brain. It resolves when the drug is stopped.

vignette: A 24-year-old man has 8 months of low back and buttock pain with stiffness that lasts over an hour each morning, improves with exercise, and wakes him in the second half of the night. Forward bending of the spine is reduced.
stem: Which of the following is the best initial test?
explanation: X-ray of the sacroiliac joints.

Inflammatory back pain in a young man suggests ankylosing spondylitis. Plain films showing sacroiliitis are the first test; MRI is used if films are normal and suspicion remains. HLA-B27 supports but does not make the diagnosis.

vignette: A 74-year-old woman has an acutely swollen, painful knee. X-ray shows calcification within the joint cartilage.
stem: Which finding is expected in the joint fluid?

options.label: E
options.text: Clear fluid with fewer than 200 white cells

explanation: Rhomboid, positively birefringent crystals.

Calcium pyrophosphate deposition (pseudogout) often affects the knee or wrist in older adults, with cartilage calcification on X-ray. In younger patients look for hemochromatosis, hyperparathyroidism, and low magnesium.

vignette: A 70-year-old woman has 6 weeks of aching and morning stiffness in both shoulders and hips, with difficulty getting out of a chair because of pain. Muscle strength is normal. ESR is 70 mm/h; creatine kinase is normal. She has no headache or visual symptoms.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Low-dose prednisone.

Polymyalgia rheumatica causes pain and stiffness, not true weakness, with a high ESR and normal muscle enzymes. Response to 10–20 mg of prednisone is rapid. High doses are for accompanying giant cell arteritis.

vignette: A 48-year-old woman with diffuse systemic sclerosis has new headaches and blood pressure of 196/118 mm Hg. Creatinine has risen from 0.9 to 2.6 mg/dL in 2 weeks. Urinalysis shows mild protein only.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: ACE inhibitor.
Scleroderma renal crisis presents with sudden severe hypertension and falling kidney function. ACE inhibitors greatly improved survival. Recent high-dose steroid use is a risk factor.

vignette: A 47-year-old man has months of bloody nasal discharge and sinus pain, now with coughing up blood. Chest imaging shows cavitating nodules. Urinalysis shows red cell casts.
stem: Which antibody is most likely to be present?
explanation: c-ANCA.

Granulomatosis with polyangiitis affects the upper airway, lungs, and kidneys. Anti-GBM disease affects lungs and kidneys but not the sinuses. Treatment is glucocorticoids with rituximab or cyclophosphamide.

vignette: A 30-year-old woman has a deep vein thrombosis of the leg. She has had three first-trimester miscarriages. Platelets are 110,000/mm³, and the PTT is prolonged and does not correct when mixed with normal plasma. Repeat testing 12 weeks later is unchanged. She is not pregnant.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate long-term treatment?
explanation: Long-term warfarin.

Antiphospholipid syndrome is clotting or pregnancy loss with a persistent antiphospholipid antibody (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, or anti–β2-glycoprotein I) on two tests 12 weeks apart. The lupus anticoagulant prolongs the PTT in the test tube but causes clotting in the body. Warfarin is preferred over direct oral anticoagulants; in pregnancy, heparin plus aspirin is used.

vignette: A 27-year-old man is stung by a bee. Ten minutes later he has widespread hives, wheezing, lip swelling, and blood pressure of 82/50 mm Hg.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate treatment?

options.label: C
options.text: Intramuscular epinephrine in the outer thigh

explanation: Intramuscular epinephrine.

Epinephrine into the outer thigh is the first and only life-saving drug in anaphylaxis; absorption is faster than from a subcutaneous injection. Antihistamines and steroids are add-ons and never replace it.

vignette: A 60-year-old man who started lisinopril 3 weeks ago has swelling of the lips and tongue. There are no hives or itching.
stem: Which of the following best explains this reaction?
explanation: Bradykinin.

ACE normally breaks down bradykinin. ACE inhibitor angioedema has no hives or itch, can appear weeks to years after starting, and does not respond reliably to antihistamines or epinephrine. The drug is stopped permanently and the airway watched.

vignette: A 19-year-old woman has recurrent episodes of swelling of the face and hands without hives, and bouts of severe abdominal pain. Her father has similar episodes. Antihistamines do not help. C4 is low.
stem: Which of the following is the most likely cause?
explanation: C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency.

Hereditary angioedema is autosomal dominant, bradykinin-driven, and causes swelling of skin, gut, and airway without hives. C4 is low. Attacks are treated with C1 inhibitor concentrate, icatibant, or ecallantide. ACE inhibitors are avoided.

vignette: A 28-year-old man has had four episodes of sinusitis and two pneumonias in 2 years, and chronic diarrhea from Giardia. IgG, IgA, and IgM are all low. B-cell count is normal. Response to vaccines is poor.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Immunoglobulin replacement.

Common variable immunodeficiency presents in young adults with recurrent sinus and lung infections, Giardia, low immunoglobulins, and poor vaccine response, with B cells present but not maturing. Risk of autoimmune disease and lymphoma is raised.

vignette: A 34-year-old woman with recurrent sinus infections and celiac disease receives a red cell transfusion. Within minutes she has hives, wheezing, and hypotension.
stem: Which of the following is the most likely underlying condition?
explanation: Selective IgA deficiency.

It is the most common primary immunodeficiency and often silent. Some patients have sinus and gut infections and autoimmune disease such as celiac disease. Those with anti-IgA antibodies can have anaphylaxis to blood products containing IgA.

vignette: A 9-month-old boy has had three episodes of otitis media and two pneumonias since age 6 months. Tonsils are not visible and no lymph nodes are felt. All immunoglobulin classes are very low, and CD19-positive cells are absent. A maternal uncle died of infection in childhood.
stem: Which gene is most likely affected?
explanation: Bruton tyrosine kinase.

X-linked agammaglobulinemia appears in boys after about 6 months, when maternal antibody fades. B cells are absent, so tonsils and nodes are small or missing. Treatment is immunoglobulin replacement; live vaccines are avoided.

vignette: A 4-year-old boy has had recurrent skin abscesses from Staphylococcus aureus, a liver abscess, and pneumonia from Aspergillus.
stem: Which test is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?
explanation: Dihydrorhodamine flow cytometry.

Chronic granulomatous disease is a defect of NADPH oxidase: phagocytes cannot make the oxidative burst and fail to kill catalase-positive organisms (Staphylococcus aureus, Aspergillus, Serratia, Nocardia, Burkholderia).

vignette: A 25-year-old woman has sneezing, itchy nose, nasal blockage, and clear discharge every spring. Nasal lining is pale and swollen.
stem: Which single treatment is most effective?
explanation: Intranasal corticosteroid.
It is the most effective single treatment for allergic rhinitis, including for blockage. Topical decongestants used for more than 3 days cause rebound congestion.

vignette: A 9-year-old boy finishes a course of cefaclor. Eight days after starting it he develops fever, an itchy hive-like rash, and pain in several joints. Urinalysis shows mild protein. C3 and C4 are low.
stem: Which type of reaction is this?
explanation: Type III.

Serum sickness-like reactions occur 1–2 weeks after exposure to a drug or foreign protein, with fever, rash, joint pain, and low complement from immune complexes. Treatment is stopping the drug and symptom relief.

vignette: A 3-day-old infant has seizures. Calcium is 6.1 mg/dL. Echocardiogram shows truncus arteriosus, and chest X-ray shows no thymic shadow. The infant has low-set ears and a small jaw.
stem: Which of the following is the most likely cause?

options.label: A
options.text: Defect in the common gamma chain

explanation: 22q11.2 deletion.
DiGeorge syndrome results from failed development of the third and fourth pharyngeal pouches: absent thymus (T-cell deficiency), absent parathyroids (low calcium), and outflow-tract heart defects.

vignette: A 54-year-old woman returns for the result of a breast biopsy, which shows invasive cancer. She is seated in a private room with her husband.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate way to begin?

options.label: B
options.text: "Let's talk about surgery and chemotherapy options."

options.label: C
options.text: "What is your understanding of why we did the biopsy?"

options.label: E
options.text: "I'd like the oncologist to give you the results."

explanation: Ask what the patient already understands.

In the SPIKES approach: Setting, Perception, Invitation, Knowledge, Emotions, Strategy. After the setting is arranged, the clinician finds out what the patient knows and how much they want to hear before giving the news.

vignette: A physician discovers that a hospitalized patient received twice the ordered dose of a blood pressure medication yesterday because of an order-entry mistake. The patient had no symptoms and vital signs remained normal.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.label: A
options.text: Tell the patient about the error, apologize, and explain what will be done to prevent it happening again

options.label: B
options.text: Document the error in the chart but tell the patient only if asked

options.label: C
options.text: Report it to the pharmacy and say nothing, since no harm occurred

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the hospital's legal department whether to tell the patient

options.label: E
options.text: Tell the patient's family instead of the patient

explanation: Disclose and apologize.
Patients are told about errors in their care whether or not harm resulted. Honest disclosure respects autonomy and maintains trust. The error is also reported through the hospital's safety system.

vignette: A surgery resident notices that an attending surgeon smells of alcohol and has slurred speech just before a scheduled operation.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.label: A
options.text: Say nothing, because the attending is senior

options.label: B
options.text: Offer the attending coffee and proceed

options.label: C
options.text: Tell the patient privately and let the patient decide

options.label: D
options.text: Wait to see whether the attending makes an error

options.label: E
options.text: Make sure the attending does not operate, and report to the department chair or physician health program

explanation: Protect the patient and report.
Patient safety comes first: an impaired physician must not provide care. Physicians have a duty to report impaired colleagues through the proper channel, which also gets the colleague help.

vignette: A 16-year-old girl comes to clinic alone and asks for contraception. She is sexually active with a boyfriend her own age and asks that her parents not be told.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

options.label: A
options.text: Tell her parental consent is required

options.label: C
options.text: Call her parents after the visit

explanation: Confidential care.

Minors can generally consent on their own to contraception, pregnancy care, treatment of sexually transmitted infections, and in many places substance use and mental health care. Encourage, but do not require, talking with parents.

vignette: A 68-year-old man who speaks only Spanish is being consented for cardiac catheterization. His adult daughter, who is bilingual, offers to translate.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.label: B
options.text: Use a translation app on a phone

options.label: C
options.text: Have the patient sign the form and explain later

options.label: E
options.text: Ask a bilingual member of the cleaning staff

explanation: Professional interpreter.
Family members may leave out, soften, or alter information and their presence compromises privacy. Trained interpreters, in person or by phone or video, are the standard for consent discussions.

vignette: A 7-year-old boy is bleeding heavily after a car crash and will die without a blood transfusion. His parents are Jehovah's Witnesses and refuse transfusion on religious grounds. There is no time to obtain a court order.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the hospital chaplain to persuade the parents

options.label: E
options.text: Transfer the child to another hospital

explanation: Transfuse.

Parents may not refuse life-saving treatment for a child. In an emergency the physician treats without waiting for a court order. A competent adult Jehovah's Witness, in contrast, may refuse blood for themselves.

vignette: A 79-year-old man with mild dementia has a gangrenous toe and refuses amputation. He explains that he understands the infection could spread and kill him, that surgery would likely prevent this, and that he would rather accept that risk than lose part of his foot. His son demands the surgery be done.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.label: A
options.text: Proceed with surgery on the son's consent

options.label: C
options.text: Request psychiatric consultation before any decision

options.label: E
options.text: Respect the patient's refusal and offer other care

explanation: Respect the refusal.

Capacity is specific to the decision: the patient must understand the facts, appreciate how they apply to him, reason about the options, and express a choice. A diagnosis of dementia does not by itself remove capacity, and any physician can assess it.

vignette: A 34-year-old patient tells her primary care physician at the end of a visit that she finds him attractive and asks him to dinner. The physician is single.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

options.label: A
options.text: Accept, since both are consenting adults

options.label: B
options.text: Decline, and explain that a romantic relationship with a patient is not appropriate

options.label: C
options.text: Accept, but transfer her care first

options.label: D
options.text: Ignore the comment and leave the room

options.label: E
options.text: Suggest waiting until the next appointment to discuss

explanation: Decline.

Romantic or sexual relationships with current patients are never appropriate, because of the power imbalance and the risk to the patient's care. The boundary is stated kindly and clearly and care continues.

vignette: The daughter of an 81-year-old man asks the physician not to tell her father that his scan shows metastatic cancer, saying, "It would destroy him." The patient is alert and has decision-making capacity.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

options.label: B
options.text: Tell the daughter this request is unethical and end the discussion

options.label: C
options.text: Tell the patient immediately while the daughter is out of the room

options.label: D
options.text: Explore the daughter's concerns, then ask the patient how much he wants to know

options.label: E
options.text: Ask the ethics committee to decide

explanation: Explore, then ask the patient.

Families usually make this request out of love. Understanding their fear comes first. But a patient with capacity has the right to their own medical information, and the right to decline it, so the physician asks the patient how much he wants to know and who should be involved.

vignette: A 73-year-old woman with end-stage lung disease has a written living will stating she does not want intubation. She is now unresponsive with respiratory failure. Her husband says, "Do everything, put her on the machine."
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.label: A
options.text: Follow the living will and provide comfort-focused care

options.label: B
options.text: Intubate, because the husband is the surrogate

options.label: C
options.text: Intubate for 48 hours as a compromise

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the couple's children to vote

explanation: Follow the living will.

A patient's own clearly stated wishes outrank a surrogate's preferences. The surrogate's role is to say what the patient would have wanted, not what the surrogate wants. The husband needs compassionate explanation and support.

vignette: A 64-year-old man on dialysis missed two sessions. Potassium is 7.4 mEq/L. ECG shows tall peaked T waves and a widened QRS.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate first step?
explanation: IV calcium gluconate.

With ECG changes, calcium is given first to stabilize the heart muscle; it works in minutes but does not lower potassium. Insulin with glucose and albuterol then shift potassium into cells, and dialysis removes it.

vignette: A 52-year-old woman is brought in after a seizure. Sodium is 112 mEq/L. She remains confused.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.label: B
options.text: Bolus of 3% saline, raising sodium by no more than about 8 mEq/L in 24 hours

options.label: C
options.text: Normal saline at 500 mL/h until sodium is 135 mEq/L

explanation: Hypertonic saline with a controlled rise.
Severe symptoms (seizure, coma) call for 3% saline boluses to raise sodium by 4–6 mEq/L quickly. The total rise is kept to about 8 mEq/L in 24 hours to avoid osmotic demyelination.

vignette: A 66-year-old man with small cell lung cancer has sodium of 124 mEq/L and mild nausea. He appears normally hydrated. Serum osmolality is 258 mOsm/kg, urine osmolality 480 mOsm/kg, urine sodium 45 mEq/L. Thyroid and adrenal tests are normal.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
explanation: Fluid restriction.

This is the syndrome of inappropriate ADH: low serum osmolality, urine that is not maximally dilute, urine sodium above 40, and normal volume. Normal saline can make it worse because the salt is excreted and the water kept.

vignette: A 70-year-old man had prolonged hypotension during surgery for a ruptured aortic aneurysm. Two days later creatinine has risen from 1.0 to 3.4 mg/dL. Urine sodium is 52 mEq/L and fractional excretion of sodium is 3%.
stem: Which urine finding is most likely?
explanation: Muddy brown granular casts.

Ischemic acute tubular necrosis follows prolonged low blood pressure. Damaged tubules cannot reabsorb sodium, so fractional excretion is above 2%. Prerenal injury gives a value below 1% and bland urine.

vignette: A 7-year-old boy has cola-colored urine, puffy eyelids, and blood pressure of 138/90 mm Hg. He had impetigo 3 weeks ago. Urinalysis shows red cell casts.
stem: Which laboratory finding is most likely?
explanation: Low C3.

Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis follows throat infection by 1–2 weeks or skin infection by 3–6 weeks. C3 is low and returns to normal within about 8 weeks. Treatment is supportive. IgA nephropathy, in contrast, appears within days of an infection, with normal complement.

vignette: A 4-year-old boy has swelling of the face and legs for a week. Urinalysis shows 4+ protein and no blood. Albumin is 1.8 g/dL, cholesterol is high, creatinine and complement are normal, and blood pressure is normal.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: Oral prednisone.

Nephrotic syndrome in a young child with no blood in the urine, normal blood pressure, and normal complement is presumed minimal change disease and treated with steroids without biopsy. Biopsy is for those who do not respond or have atypical features.

vignette: A 28-year-old man is found after lying on the floor for 18 hours following a drug overdose. Urine is dark brown; dipstick is strongly positive for blood, but microscopy shows no red cells. Creatine kinase is 48,000 U/L.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Aggressive IV saline.
Dipstick positive for blood without red cells means myoglobin. Rhabdomyolysis damages the kidney tubules; early large-volume fluids are the main protection. Watch for high potassium and low calcium.

vignette: A 45-year-old man is brought in confused. pH is 7.14, bicarbonate 8 mEq/L, anion gap 28, and the osmolal gap is raised. Glucose, lactate, and ketones are normal. Urine shows envelope-shaped crystals.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Fomepizole.

A high anion gap with a high osmolal gap and calcium oxalate crystals indicates ethylene glycol poisoning. Fomepizole blocks alcohol dehydrogenase so toxic acids are not formed. Dialysis is added for severe acidosis or kidney injury.

vignette: A 50-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 180 mg/g on two tests 3 months apart. Blood pressure is 142/88 mm Hg and eGFR is 72 mL/min/1.73 m².
stem: Which medication is most appropriate to start?
explanation: ACE inhibitor.

In diabetes with albuminuria, an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker lowers pressure inside the glomerulus and slows kidney disease. An SGLT2 inhibitor is also recommended. Creatinine and potassium are checked 1–2 weeks after starting.

vignette: A 26-year-old woman at 16 weeks of pregnancy has no urinary symptoms. Routine urine culture grows more than 100,000 colonies/mL of Escherichia coli.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.label: A
options.text: No treatment, since she has no symptoms

explanation: Cephalexin.

Bacteria in the urine without symptoms are treated in pregnancy because the risk of pyelonephritis and preterm birth is high. Fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines are avoided. A repeat culture confirms clearance.

vignette: A 52-year-old man has fatigue. Hemoglobin is 9.4 g/dL, MCV 72 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL. He has no visible bleeding and eats a normal diet.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step, besides iron replacement?
explanation: Colonoscopy.
Iron deficiency in a man or a postmenopausal woman is from gut blood loss until proven otherwise; colon cancer must be excluded. Upper endoscopy is usually done at the same time.

vignette: A 63-year-old woman has received unfractionated heparin for 7 days after hip surgery. Platelets have fallen from 240,000 to 90,000/mm³ and she has a new deep vein thrombosis.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.label: D
options.text: Stop heparin and start warfarin alone

explanation: Stop heparin, start a non-heparin anticoagulant.

Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia appears 5–10 days after starting, with a platelet fall of more than half and clotting rather than bleeding. All heparin, including low-molecular-weight, is stopped. Warfarin is not started until platelets recover, because early warfarin can cause skin necrosis and limb gangrene.

vignette: A 36-year-old woman has confusion, fever, and bruising. Hemoglobin is 7.8 g/dL, platelets 18,000/mm³, creatinine 1.9 mg/dL, LDH high. Blood film shows fragmented red cells. PT and PTT are normal.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Plasma exchange.

Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura is from deficient ADAMTS13. Fragmented red cells and low platelets with normal clotting times separate it from disseminated intravascular coagulation. Plasma exchange is started on suspicion; platelet transfusion is avoided unless bleeding is life-threatening.

vignette: A 22-year-old man with sickle cell disease has had four admissions for pain crises in the past year.
stem: Which treatment will most reduce the frequency of crises?
explanation: Hydroxyurea.
It raises fetal hemoglobin, reducing sickling, pain crises, acute chest syndrome, and deaths. Folic acid supports red cell production but does not prevent crises.

vignette: A 67-year-old woman has fatigue, a sore smooth tongue, numbness of the feet, and loss of vibration sense. Hemoglobin is 8.6 g/dL, MCV 118 fL.
stem: Which set of results is expected?
explanation: Both raised.

B12 is needed to convert methylmalonyl-CoA and to convert homocysteine to methionine, so both build up. In folate deficiency only homocysteine rises, and there are no nerve signs. Pernicious anemia is the most common cause.

vignette: A 31-year-old woman has nosebleeds and small red spots on her legs. Platelets are 12,000/mm³; hemoglobin, white count, blood film, and clotting tests are otherwise normal. The spleen is not enlarged. HIV and hepatitis C tests are negative.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Glucocorticoids.

Immune thrombocytopenia is isolated low platelets with no other cause. Adults are treated when platelets are below 30,000/mm³ or there is bleeding. Immunoglobulin is added when a rapid rise is needed.

vignette: A 70-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer is starting scheduled morphine for bone pain.
stem: Which of the following should be prescribed at the same time?
explanation: Senna.
Constipation is the one opioid side effect to which patients do not develop tolerance, so a stimulant laxative is started with the opioid. Fiber alone can worsen it.

vignette: A 76-year-old woman with terminal lung cancer in hospice is distressed by breathlessness at rest. Oxygen saturation is 93% on room air. She is not anxious and has no reversible cause.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Low-dose morphine.
Opioids are the best treatment for breathlessness at the end of life and, at careful doses, do not shorten life. Oxygen helps only when blood oxygen is low. A fan blowing on the face also helps.

vignette: A 78-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic cancer has declined further chemotherapy. He is in bed most of the day and wants to be at home, comfortable, with his family.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate recommendation?

options.label: D
options.text: Transfer to a nursing facility for rehabilitation

explanation: Hospice.

Hospice is for patients with an expected survival of 6 months or less who choose comfort over disease-directed treatment. It provides care at home, medicines and equipment, and support for the family, including after death.

vignette: A 59-year-old woman with breast cancer spread to bone takes one oxycodone-acetaminophen tablet every 4 hours around the clock and still rates her pain 8 out of 10.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate change?

options.label: B
options.text: Switch to a long-acting opioid with a short-acting opioid for breakthrough pain

options.label: D
options.text: Continue the same regimen and reassess in a month

options.label: E
options.text: Stop opioids because of the risk of addiction

explanation: Long-acting opioid with breakthrough doses.

Constant severe cancer pain needs a scheduled long-acting opioid, with a short-acting dose of roughly 10–15% of the daily total for breakthrough pain. Combination tablets are limited by the acetaminophen content. Addiction concern should not lead to undertreated cancer pain.

vignette: A 24-year-old man started chemotherapy for Burkitt lymphoma 2 days ago. Potassium is 6.1 mEq/L, phosphate 8.2 mg/dL, calcium 6.8 mg/dL, uric acid 14 mg/dL, creatinine 2.3 mg/dL. IV fluids are running.
stem: Which medication is most appropriate to add?
explanation: Rasburicase.

Tumor lysis syndrome releases cell contents: high potassium, phosphate, and uric acid, with low calcium and kidney injury. Allopurinol prevents new uric acid forming but does not remove what is there; rasburicase breaks it down. It is avoided in G6PD deficiency. Low calcium is treated only if symptomatic.

vignette: A 55-year-old woman had chemotherapy for leukemia 9 days ago. Temperature is 38.6°C. Absolute neutrophil count is 300/mm³. She has no localizing symptoms and looks well.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: A
options.text: Blood cultures and observe without antibiotics

options.label: D
options.text: Blood cultures and immediate IV cefepime

explanation: Cultures and immediate anti-pseudomonal antibiotic.

Fever with a neutrophil count below 500/mm³ is an emergency. Signs of infection are often absent. A broad antibiotic covering Pseudomonas (cefepime, piperacillin-tazobactam, or a carbapenem) is given within an hour.

vignette: A 61-year-old woman with breast cancer has 2 weeks of worsening mid-back pain, now with leg weakness and difficulty urinating since yesterday.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate step?
explanation: IV dexamethasone.

Back pain with new neurologic signs in a cancer patient is spinal cord compression until excluded. Steroids are given at once, then urgent MRI of the whole spine, then surgery or radiation. Function at the start of treatment predicts outcome.

vignette: A 64-year-old man with squamous cell lung cancer is confused, constipated, and passing large amounts of urine. Calcium is 14.8 mg/dL and PTH is suppressed.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
explanation: IV normal saline.

Hypercalcemia of malignancy, here from PTH-related peptide, causes volume loss through heavy urination. Fluids come first; calcitonin acts fast and an IV bisphosphonate gives a lasting effect. Loop diuretics are used only for fluid overload, and thiazides raise calcium.

vignette: A 58-year-old man has smoked a pack a day for 30 years and still smokes. He has no symptoms.
stem: Which screening test is recommended?
explanation: Annual low-dose CT.
Screening is recommended for adults aged 50–80 with at least 20 pack-years who smoke now or quit within the past 15 years. Chest X-ray screening does not reduce deaths.

vignette: A 36-year-old man asks about colon cancer screening. His father was diagnosed with colon cancer at age 52. No other relatives are affected.
stem: When should he begin colonoscopy?
explanation: Age 40.

With a first-degree relative diagnosed before 60, colonoscopy starts at 40 or 10 years before the relative's age at diagnosis, whichever is earlier, and is repeated every 5 years. Here 10 years earlier would be 42, so 40 applies.

vignette: A 45-year-old woman feels a firm lump in her left breast. Mammogram and ultrasound show a 1.8-cm irregular mass with spiculated margins.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: B
options.text: Excision of the mass with wide margins

explanation: Core needle biopsy.
A suspicious breast mass needs a tissue diagnosis before any surgery. Core biopsy gives histology and receptor status (estrogen, progesterone, HER2), which guide treatment.

vignette: A 50-year-old man has fatigue and fullness in the left upper abdomen. White cell count is 142,000/mm³ with neutrophils at all stages of maturation and increased basophils. The spleen is enlarged. Genetic testing shows a t(9;22) translocation.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Imatinib.

Chronic myeloid leukemia carries the Philadelphia chromosome, producing the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors give long-term control. A low leukocyte alkaline phosphatase score separates it from a reactive high white count.

vignette: A 26-year-old woman has a painless, rubbery 3-cm lymph node in the neck for 6 weeks, with night sweats, weight loss, and generalized itching. Chest X-ray shows a wide mediastinum.
stem: Which of the following is the best test to establish the diagnosis?
explanation: Excisional lymph node biopsy.

Lymphoma diagnosis needs the node's architecture; fine-needle aspiration is not enough. The picture suggests Hodgkin lymphoma, where Reed–Sternberg cells are scattered among reactive cells. PET is used for staging after diagnosis.

vignette: A 68-year-old man has 3 months of back pain and fatigue. Hemoglobin is 9.2 g/dL, calcium 11.8 mg/dL, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, total protein high with normal albumin. Spine X-ray shows punched-out lytic lesions.
stem: Which of the following is the best next test?

options.label: E
options.text: Serum protein electrophoresis with free light chains

explanation: Serum protein electrophoresis with free light chains.

High calcium, kidney injury, anemia, and lytic bone lesions suggest multiple myeloma. Bone scan is often negative because lesions are purely lytic, and alkaline phosphatase is usually normal. Bone marrow biopsy confirms.

vignette: A 34-year-old woman with untreated Graves disease is brought in 1 day after an appendectomy. Temperature is 40.1°C, pulse 152/min and irregular, and she is agitated and confused.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.label: C
options.text: Potassium iodide first, then propylthiouracil an hour later

options.label: D
options.text: Propranolol and propylthiouracil, with iodine given at least an hour after the propylthiouracil

explanation: Block hormone action and synthesis first, then give iodine.

Thyroid storm is treated with a beta blocker, a thionamide (propylthiouracil also blocks T4-to-T3 conversion), iodine given at least an hour after the thionamide so it is not used to make more hormone, and glucocorticoids. Aspirin is avoided because it frees thyroid hormone from its binding proteins; acetaminophen is used for fever.

vignette: A 78-year-old woman is found at home confused. Temperature is 34.2°C, pulse 46/min, sodium 124 mEq/L. Her face is puffy and reflexes are slow to relax. TSH is 68 μU/mL and free T4 is very low.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.label: E
options.text: Oral levothyroxine at a low starting dose

explanation: IV levothyroxine with hydrocortisone.

Myxedema coma is severe hypothyroidism with hypothermia, low sodium, slow heart rate, and confusion, and it is often fatal. Thyroid hormone is given IV, and stress-dose hydrocortisone is given until coexisting adrenal insufficiency is excluded, because thyroid hormone can provoke adrenal crisis.

vignette: A 27-year-old woman at 8 weeks of pregnancy has palpitations, weight loss, and a diffuse goiter. TSH is suppressed and free T4 is high. Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin is positive.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Propylthiouracil in the first trimester.

Methimazole can cause birth defects (such as scalp aplasia cutis) when used in early pregnancy, so propylthiouracil is used until about 16 weeks, then switched to methimazole because of propylthiouracil's liver toxicity. Radioactive iodine is contraindicated in pregnancy.

vignette: A 74-year-old man with type 2 diabetes is brought in drowsy after a week of increased thirst and urination. Glucose is 1,100 mg/dL, serum osmolality 360 mOsm/kg, pH 7.36, bicarbonate 24 mEq/L, and serum ketones are negative.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate first step?
explanation: Rapid IV normal saline.

Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state causes severe dehydration, often 8–10 L. Isotonic fluid is the first and most important step; insulin is started after fluids are running and potassium is known, and fluid alone lowers glucose substantially.

vignette: A 31-year-old nurse is brought in after fainting at work. Glucose is 38 mg/dL. At the time of hypoglycemia, insulin is high, C-peptide is low, and proinsulin is low. A sulfonylurea screen is negative.
stem: Which of the following is the most likely cause?
explanation: Surreptitious insulin.

Injected insulin raises insulin but suppresses the pancreas, so C-peptide (released with natural insulin) is low. Insulinoma and sulfonylureas raise both insulin and C-peptide. Healthcare workers have access to insulin.

vignette: A 46-year-old woman has episodes of confusion and sweating that resolve with food. During a supervised fast, glucose falls to 42 mg/dL with high insulin, high C-peptide, and high proinsulin.
stem: Which test should be done next?

options.label: B
options.text: CT of the pancreas without further testing

explanation: Sulfonylurea screen.

High insulin, C-peptide, and proinsulin with hypoglycemia means the pancreas is overproducing insulin, either from an insulinoma or from a sulfonylurea or meglitinide. Only a drug screen tells them apart, and it must be negative before imaging for insulinoma.

vignette: A 32-year-old man has a thyroid nodule. Fine-needle aspiration shows medullary thyroid carcinoma. His father had a thyroid tumor and an adrenal tumor.
stem: Which test must be done before thyroidectomy?
explanation: Plasma free metanephrines.

Medullary thyroid cancer with a family history of adrenal tumors suggests MEN 2 (RET mutation). A pheochromocytoma must be ruled out and removed first, because operating on the thyroid with an untreated pheochromocytoma can cause a hypertensive crisis.

vignette: A 52-year-old woman has calcium of 11.6 mg/dL (upper limit 10.2) and a high PTH on two occasions. She has no symptoms. Bone density T-score is −1.6, eGFR is 85 mL/min/1.73 m², and she has no kidney stones.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.label: B
options.text: Observation with yearly calcium and creatinine

explanation: Parathyroidectomy.

Surgery is advised in asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism when calcium is more than 1 mg/dL above the upper limit, T-score is −2.5 or lower, eGFR is below 60, there are kidney stones or high urine calcium, or age is under 50. Her calcium is 1.4 mg/dL above the limit.

vignette: A 44-year-old woman had a total thyroidectomy yesterday. She now has tingling around the mouth and fingers. Tapping the face in front of the ear causes twitching of the lip. Calcium is 6.9 mg/dL.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.label: C
options.text: Observation and repeat calcium in 24 hours

explanation: IV calcium gluconate.

Symptomatic hypocalcemia after thyroidectomy (from parathyroid injury or removal) with a positive Chvostek sign is treated with IV calcium. Oral calcium and calcitriol are then started, and magnesium is checked and corrected.

vignette: A 29-year-old man has had heavy urination and thirst since a head injury 3 weeks ago. Sodium is 149 mEq/L and urine osmolality is 110 mOsm/kg. After water deprivation, urine osmolality stays at 130 mOsm/kg. After desmopressin, it rises to 450 mOsm/kg.
stem: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Central diabetes insipidus.

Dilute urine that does not concentrate with dehydration but does concentrate after desmopressin means the kidney works but ADH is missing. Head trauma, pituitary surgery, and tumors are common causes. In nephrogenic DI, desmopressin produces little change.

vignette: A 52-year-old woman with bipolar disorder has taken lithium for 15 years. She now passes 6 L of urine a day. Urine osmolality does not rise with water deprivation or with desmopressin. Lithium must be continued.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Amiloride.

Lithium enters collecting-duct cells through the sodium channel and causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. Amiloride blocks that channel and reduces urine output; thiazides also help. Desmopressin does not work because the kidney cannot respond to ADH.

vignette: A 45-year-old man has noticed his ring and shoe sizes increasing. He has headaches, a large jaw with widely spaced teeth, and coarse facial features.
stem: Which of the following is the best initial test?
explanation: Insulin-like growth factor 1.

IGF-1 reflects average growth hormone over time and is the best screening test for acromegaly. A random GH level is unreliable because GH is released in pulses. A high IGF-1 is confirmed by failure of GH to suppress after an oral glucose load, then pituitary MRI.

vignette: A 31-year-old woman had a severe postpartum hemorrhage requiring transfusion 4 months ago. She could not breastfeed, her periods have not returned, and she is tired and cold.
stem: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Sheehan syndrome.

The pituitary enlarges in pregnancy and is vulnerable to infarction with severe blood loss. Failure to lactate (no prolactin) is often the first sign, followed by amenorrhea, hypothyroidism, and adrenal insufficiency. Cortisol replacement is started before thyroid hormone.

vignette: A 58-year-old man has a 2.5-cm left adrenal mass found on CT for abdominal pain. It is uniform, smooth, and of low density (8 Hounsfield units). Blood pressure and potassium are normal.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: B
options.text: Overnight 1-mg dexamethasone suppression test and plasma metanephrines

explanation: Hormone testing.

Every adrenal incidentaloma is checked for cortisol excess (1-mg dexamethasone suppression) and pheochromocytoma (metanephrines), and for aldosterone excess if there is hypertension or low potassium. A small, uniform, low-density mass is benign-looking, so no repeat imaging is usually needed if hormone tests are normal.

vignette: A 2-week-old girl has vomiting, poor feeding, and ambiguous genitalia with an enlarged clitoris. Sodium is 128 mEq/L and potassium 6.8 mEq/L.
stem: Which laboratory finding is most likely?
explanation: High 17-hydroxyprogesterone.

21-hydroxylase deficiency is the most common form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Cortisol and aldosterone cannot be made, so ACTH rises, precursors are diverted to androgens (virilizing girls), and salt wasting causes low sodium and high potassium.

vignette: A 29-year-old woman at 9 weeks of pregnancy has TSH of 6.8 μU/mL with normal free T4. Anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies are positive. She feels well.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
explanation: Start levothyroxine.

In pregnancy, a TSH above the trimester-specific range with positive TPO antibodies is treated, because untreated hypothyroidism is linked to miscarriage and impaired fetal brain development. Thyroid hormone needs rise in pregnancy.

vignette: A 76-year-old man with stable coronary artery disease has fatigue and constipation. TSH is 22 μU/mL and free T4 is low.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.label: A
options.text: No treatment until he has symptoms of heart failure

options.label: C
options.text: Full replacement dose of levothyroxine based on weight

explanation: Start low and go slow.

In older adults and those with coronary disease, a full dose can increase heart oxygen demand and trigger angina or arrhythmia. Levothyroxine is started at about 12.5–25 μg daily and increased every 4–6 weeks based on TSH.

vignette: A 30-year-old woman at 26 weeks of pregnancy has a 1-hour glucose level of 162 mg/dL after a 50-g oral glucose load.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: 3-hour glucose tolerance test.

In the two-step approach, an abnormal 1-hour screen (commonly 130–140 mg/dL or higher) is followed by a diagnostic 3-hour 100-g test. Gestational diabetes is diagnosed if two or more values are high. Treatment starts only after diagnosis.

vignette: A 48-year-old man with obesity has an HbA1c of 6.7% on routine testing. He has no symptoms and a random glucose of 132 mg/dL.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: C
options.text: Repeat HbA1c or a fasting glucose to confirm

explanation: Confirm with a repeat test.

In someone without clear symptoms, diabetes is diagnosed by two abnormal results, either the same test repeated or two different tests. A single HbA1c of 6.5% or higher is not enough unless glucose is clearly high (200 mg/dL or more) with typical symptoms.

vignette: A 62-year-old woman has taken prednisone 20 mg daily for 6 months for polymyalgia rheumatica. She is scheduled for a colectomy.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate perioperative plan?

options.label: A
options.text: Stress-dose IV hydrocortisone around surgery, then taper back to her usual dose

options.label: D
options.text: Continue the usual dose only, with no added steroid

options.label: E
options.text: Check a cosyntropin test and delay surgery for the result

explanation: Stress-dose steroids.

Anyone taking 20 mg or more of prednisone for more than 3 weeks should be assumed to have adrenal suppression. Major surgery calls for stress-dose hydrocortisone around the operation, then a return to the usual dose. Stopping steroids beforehand risks adrenal crisis.

vignette: A 47-year-old man has a new right-sided scrotal swelling that feels like a bag of worms. It does not shrink when he lies down.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: CT scan of the abdomen.

Most varicoceles are left-sided because the left testicular vein drains at a right angle into the left renal vein. A new right-sided or non-reducing varicocele raises concern for a retroperitoneal or renal mass compressing the vein.

vignette: A 38-year-old man has a painless, smooth swelling of the left scrotum that has grown over 3 months. It transilluminates, and the testis cannot be felt separately.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: Scrotal ultrasound.
A hydrocele transilluminates, but in an adult, especially if the testis cannot be felt, ultrasound is needed to exclude an underlying tumor, infection, or torsion that can cause a reactive hydrocele.

vignette: A 68-year-old man had a prostate biopsy for a PSA of 6.1 ng/mL. It shows Gleason 3+3 (grade group 1) cancer in 2 of 12 cores. He has no symptoms and wants to avoid side effects.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.label: D
options.text: External beam radiation with hormone therapy

explanation: Active surveillance.

Low-risk prostate cancer (grade group 1, low PSA, small volume) rarely progresses. Active surveillance with PSA, examination, MRI, and repeat biopsies avoids the urinary and sexual side effects of surgery or radiation while keeping cure possible.

vignette: A 61-year-old man who smokes has blood in his urine, left flank pain, and a palpable left abdominal mass. Hemoglobin is 18.4 g/dL. A left varicocele appeared recently.
stem: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.text: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder

explanation: Renal cell carcinoma.

The classic triad is flank pain, blood in the urine, and a flank mass, though few patients have all three. The tumor can make erythropoietin (high hemoglobin) and invade the left renal vein, causing a left varicocele. Smoking is the main risk factor.

vignette: A 49-year-old man with gout has a kidney stone. The stone is not seen on plain X-ray but is visible on CT. Urine pH is 5.0.
stem: Which treatment best prevents more stones?
explanation: Potassium citrate.

Uric acid stones are invisible on plain X-ray and form in acidic urine. Raising urine pH to 6–6.5 with potassium citrate dissolves and prevents them; allopurinol is added if uric acid excretion is high.

vignette: A 42-year-old woman has had three calcium oxalate stones. 24-hour urine shows high calcium.
stem: Which dietary advice is most appropriate?

options.label: B
options.text: Normal calcium intake with less sodium and animal protein

explanation: Normal calcium, less salt and animal protein.

Dietary calcium binds oxalate in the gut, so low-calcium diets increase stone risk. Sodium and animal protein increase urine calcium. High fluid intake is the most important single measure; a thiazide helps with high urine calcium.

vignette: A 66-year-old woman with recurrent urinary infections has a large branching stone filling the left renal pelvis. Urine pH is 8.0 and culture grows Proteus mirabilis.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate definitive treatment?
explanation: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy.

Struvite (staghorn) stones form in alkaline urine from urease-producing bacteria such as Proteus. The stone harbors bacteria, so it must be removed completely, and percutaneous surgery is best for large stones.

vignette: A 61-year-old man with angina takes isosorbide mononitrate daily. He asks about treatment for erectile dysfunction.
stem: Which medication must be avoided?
explanation: Tadalafil.
Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors combined with nitrates cause severe, potentially fatal low blood pressure. Other ED treatments, such as a vacuum device or alprostadil injection, can be used.

vignette: A 72-year-old woman has a sudden strong urge to urinate many times a day and often leaks before reaching the toilet. Urinalysis is normal and post-void residual is 30 mL.
stem: Which of the following is the best initial treatment?
explanation: Bladder training.

Behavioral treatment — timed voiding, urge suppression, and reducing caffeine and evening fluids — is first-line for urge incontinence. Anticholinergics are avoided where possible in older adults because of confusion, and mirabegron is an alternative.

vignette: A 45-year-old woman with three children leaks small amounts of urine when she coughs, laughs, or lifts. Urinalysis is normal.
stem: Which of the following is the best initial treatment?
explanation: Pelvic floor muscle exercises.

Stress incontinence comes from weak pelvic floor support of the urethra, often after childbirth. Kegel exercises are first-line; a mid-urethral sling is for those who do not improve. Anticholinergics treat urge, not stress, incontinence.

vignette: A 70-year-old man with long-standing diabetes and neuropathy has constant dribbling of urine. Post-void residual is 450 mL.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
explanation: Intermittent self-catheterization.
Diabetic neuropathy can leave the bladder unable to contract, so it overfills and overflows. Regular catheterization empties it and protects the kidneys. Anticholinergics would worsen retention.

vignette: A 39-year-old man has fever, chills, painful urination, and perineal pain. The prostate is very tender, warm, and swollen.
stem: Which of the following should be avoided?
explanation: Vigorous prostatic massage.

In acute bacterial prostatitis, massage is painful and can spread bacteria into the blood. Diagnosis rests on symptoms, a tender prostate, and urine culture; treatment is antibiotics such as a fluoroquinolone or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for several weeks.

vignette: A 26-year-old man has a solid testicular mass. Serum alpha-fetoprotein is markedly elevated.
stem: Which tumor type can be excluded as the only component?
explanation: Pure seminoma.
Pure seminomas never make alpha-fetoprotein. A high AFP means non-seminomatous elements, usually yolk sac tumor, are present, and the tumor is treated as non-seminomatous, which changes therapy.

vignette: An 8-month-old boy has a testis that cannot be felt in the right scrotum or groin. The left testis is normal.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.label: A
options.text: Reassurance that it will descend at puberty

explanation: Orchiopexy now.

Testes not descended by about 6 months rarely descend later. Surgery is recommended between 6 and 18 months to protect fertility and allow cancer surveillance. Hormone therapy is not recommended, and ultrasound does not change management.

vignette: A newborn boy has the urethral opening on the underside of the penis, partway down the shaft.
stem: Which of the following is the most important advice now?
explanation: Do not circumcise.

The foreskin is used to repair hypospadias, so circumcision is postponed. Repair is usually done between 6 and 18 months. Karyotyping is reserved for those with an undescended testis or ambiguous genitalia.

vignette: A 64-year-old man had a urinary catheter placed 6 hours ago. The foreskin was not returned to its normal position. The glans is now swollen and painful with a tight band behind it.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: B
options.text: Topical steroid cream and follow-up in a week

explanation: Manual reduction.

Paraphimosis is an emergency: the trapped foreskin acts as a tourniquet and can cut off blood flow to the glans. Swelling is reduced with compression or ice, then the foreskin is pushed back; if that fails, a dorsal slit is done.

vignette: A 29-year-old man has a pelvic fracture after a fall from a height. He has gross blood in the urine. There is no blood at the urethral meatus and the prostate is in normal position.
stem: Which of the following is the best test to evaluate the bladder?

options.label: E
options.text: Standard CT of the abdomen without bladder filling

explanation: Retrograde CT cystography.

Gross hematuria with a pelvic fracture suggests bladder rupture. The bladder must be actively filled with contrast to show a leak; a standard CT without filling can miss it. Extraperitoneal ruptures are often managed with a catheter, intraperitoneal ones with surgery.

vignette: A 58-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes has severe perineal pain, fever, and dusky scrotal skin with crepitus. Pain is far worse than the appearance.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.label: D
options.text: Emergency surgical debridement with broad-spectrum IV antibiotics

explanation: Emergency debridement and antibiotics.

Fournier gangrene is necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum, most common in men with diabetes. Pain out of proportion and crepitus are warning signs. It is fatal without prompt surgical removal of dead tissue; imaging must not delay surgery.

vignette: A newborn boy has bilateral hydronephrosis on prenatal ultrasound, a palpable bladder, and a weak urinary stream.
stem: Which test is best to confirm the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Voiding cystourethrogram.
