Aromatase inhibitors block estrogen production after menopause and cause bone loss and fractures. A baseline DEXA scan, calcium, vitamin D, and bisphosphonates if needed are standard. Joint pain is a common side effect.

vignette: A 62-year-old man who smokes has swelling of his face and arms, dilated veins on his chest, and shortness of breath that worsens when he bends forward. He is not in respiratory distress.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: A
options.text: CT of the chest with contrast

explanation: CT of the chest with contrast.

Superior vena cava syndrome is most often caused by lung cancer or lymphoma. In a stable patient, imaging and a tissue diagnosis come before treatment, because the right treatment depends on the type of cancer. Stenting is used for severe symptoms such as airway compromise.

vignette: A 64-year-old man who smokes has weakness in his hips and thighs and a dry mouth. His strength improves briefly after repeated effort. Chest CT shows a central lung mass.
stem: Which type of lung cancer is most likely?
explanation: Small cell carcinoma.

Lambert–Eaton syndrome results from antibodies against presynaptic calcium channels. It causes proximal weakness that improves with repeated use and autonomic symptoms such as dry mouth. It is most often linked to small cell lung cancer, which is central and associated with smoking.

vignette: A 58-year-old man who smokes has severe right shoulder pain spreading down his arm, a drooping right eyelid, a small right pupil, and loss of sweating on the right side of his face.
stem: Which of the following is the most likely cause?

options.label: C
options.text: Tumor at the top of the lung

explanation: Pancoast tumor.

A tumor at the top of the lung can invade the brachial plexus (shoulder and arm pain) and the sympathetic chain, causing Horner syndrome: ptosis, a small pupil, and loss of sweating. It is usually a non-small cell cancer.

vignette: A 48-year-old woman who has never smoked has a 1.4-cm lung nodule with a "popcorn" calcification pattern on CT.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
explanation: No further follow-up.

Popcorn calcification is characteristic of a hamartoma, a benign tumor. Benign calcification patterns (popcorn, central, laminated, or diffuse) do not need follow-up. Non-calcified nodules are managed by size and risk.

vignette: A 59-year-old man had a colon cancer resected 1 year ago.
stem: Which test is used to monitor for recurrence?
explanation: Carcinoembryonic antigen.

CEA is measured before surgery and then regularly afterwards to detect recurrence, along with CT scans and colonoscopy. It is not used for screening because it can be raised by smoking and inflammation.

vignette: A 56-year-old man has cirrhosis from hepatitis C.
stem: Which surveillance for liver cancer is recommended?

options.label: C
options.text: CT of the abdomen every month

options.label: D
options.text: Ultrasound with or without alpha-fetoprotein every 6 months

explanation: Ultrasound every 6 months.

People with cirrhosis from any cause, and some with hepatitis B without cirrhosis, should have liver ultrasound every 6 months, with or without alpha-fetoprotein, to find hepatocellular carcinoma early.

vignette: A 68-year-old man has painless jaundice, weight loss, and itching. A nontender gallbladder can be felt.
stem: Which test is most appropriate?
explanation: Pancreas-protocol CT.

Painless jaundice with a palpable, nontender gallbladder (Courvoisier sign) suggests obstruction of the bile duct by a tumor at the head of the pancreas. A dedicated CT diagnoses and stages it. CA 19-9 supports the diagnosis and is used for monitoring.

vignette: A 63-year-old woman has bloating, early fullness after meals, and increasing waist size. Examination shows ascites and a fixed pelvic mass. CA-125 is very high.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.label: C
options.text: Needle biopsy of the pelvic mass through the skin

explanation: Gynecologic oncologist.

A pelvic mass with ascites and high CA-125 in a postmenopausal woman strongly suggests ovarian cancer. Surgery for staging and maximal removal by a gynecologic oncologist improves survival. Needle biopsy through the skin risks spreading tumor cells.

vignette: A 61-year-old woman has vaginal bleeding 6 years after menopause.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: Endometrial biopsy.

Any bleeding after menopause needs evaluation for endometrial cancer. Endometrial biopsy or transvaginal ultrasound (an endometrial thickness of 4 mm or less makes cancer unlikely) is the first step. Obesity, unopposed estrogen, and tamoxifen are risk factors.

vignette: A 55-year-old man has episodes of facial flushing, watery diarrhea, and wheezing. Examination shows an enlarged liver and a murmur of tricuspid regurgitation.
stem: Which test is most appropriate?
explanation: Urine 5-HIAA.

Carcinoid syndrome occurs when a neuroendocrine tumor, usually with liver metastases, releases serotonin into the general circulation. It causes flushing, diarrhea, wheezing, and right-sided heart valve disease. 5-HIAA is a serotonin breakdown product.

vignette: A 60-year-old man has headaches and new weakness of his left arm. MRI shows three ring-enhancing lesions at the junction of gray and white matter.
stem: Which is the most likely source?
explanation: Lung cancer.

Lung cancer is the most common source of brain metastases, followed by breast cancer, melanoma, kidney cancer, and colon cancer. Metastases tend to lodge at the gray–white junction where blood vessels narrow, and are often multiple.

vignette: A 72-year-old man has an IgG M-protein of 1.4 g/dL found on routine testing. Bone marrow has 6% plasma cells. Calcium, creatinine, and hemoglobin are normal, and there are no bone lesions.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.label: D
options.text: Yearly monitoring of blood counts and M-protein

explanation: Yearly monitoring.

This is monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance: M-protein under 3 g/dL, under 10% plasma cells, and no signs of end-organ damage (high calcium, kidney injury, anemia, bone lesions). It progresses to myeloma or a related disease at about 1% a year, so it is monitored, not treated.

vignette: A 34-year-old woman has bruising and bleeding gums. The blood film shows many immature white cells with Auer rods. Fibrinogen is low and D-dimer is high. A t(15;17) translocation is found.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: All-trans retinoic acid.

Acute promyelocytic leukemia carries the t(15;17) translocation (PML-RARA). It often presents with DIC and is an emergency. ATRA, usually with arsenic trioxide, makes the cancer cells mature and has high cure rates. Treatment starts on suspicion.

vignette: A 74-year-old man has a white count of 34,000/mm³ with mostly mature lymphocytes and smudge cells on the blood film. He has no symptoms, and his hemoglobin, platelets, and spleen are normal.
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
explanation: Observation.

Chronic lymphocytic leukemia is common in older adults and often found incidentally. Early-stage disease without symptoms, low blood counts, or large nodes or spleen is monitored; early treatment does not improve survival.
